examples.before: the Company agrees to make monthly severance payments to you in the amount of $680,000

notes: Post date: (not shown). Verified against the post on 5 Nov 2026. Key quotation: "To avoid this kind of confusion, say either each or in the aggregate, depending on the meaning you intend." Source: https://www.adamsdrafting.com/a-new-variant-of-ambiguity-of-the-part-versus-the-whole/. Adams: "In five years or so, look for a section on it in the sixth edition." The post gives only the before text; the after depends on the intended meaning.

section: Blog: say-hi-to-ambiguity-of-the-specific-versus-the-general
statement: Treat ejusdem generis and including as one distinct kind of ambiguity, "ambiguity of the specific versus the general": a list of specific items followed by a general term (insects, birds, rodents, or other animals), or a general term followed by including and examples, may be read as limited to things like the specific items or as covering the whole general class.

trigger.signal: specific items followed by a general catchall, or a general term followed by examples

test: Could the general term be read as limited to things like the listed items?
fix: Apply the including rules (13.360-13.407): define the class, put the general word last with an explicit statement of scope, or list exhaustively.
notes: Post date: (not shown). Verified against the post on 5 Nov 2026. Key quotation: "I have to restructure in one respect how A Manual of Style for Contract Drafting presents ambiguity." Source: https://www.adamsdrafting.com/say-hi-to-ambiguity-of-the-specific-versus-the-general/. A structural change planned for the sixth edition (a new chapter cross-referenced from chapter 7); Adams says the analysis is already in MSCD5, so no rule changes. Related post: insects-birds-rodents-or-other-animals-ejusdem-generis-strikes-again.

section: Blog: a-new-kind-of-syntactic-ambiguity
statement: Right-node-raising pivot ambiguity: when two coordinated clauses share a final element (right node raising), it can be unclear which words the shared element (the pivot) attaches to. If you use right node raising, use offsetting commas; they aren't optional. Better still, restructure so meaning doesn't depend on the commas.

trigger.signal: two coordinated clauses that share a final element, with no offsetting commas

test: Identify the shared final element and ask whether it could attach to more or less of each clause.
fix: Add offsetting commas around each incomplete part, or repeat the shared element in each clause (12.75-12.78: don't rely on commas alone).

examples.before: The rights of all parties hereto shall be subject to the jurisdiction of and be construed according to the laws of the State of Florida, with venue in Collier County, Florida.

notes: Post date: (not shown). Verified against the post on 5 Nov 2026. Key quotation: "Commas aren't optional" Source: https://www.adamsdrafting.com/a-new-kind-of-syntactic-ambiguity/. Adams: "I'll revise that blog post and, in due course, MSCD accordingly." Terminology: Adams now calls MSCD5's "delimiting commas in coordination" (12.79-12.87) "offsetting commas in right node raising" ("Revisiting Offsetting Commas in Right Node Raising", 27 Sep 2026, https://www.adamsdrafting.com/revisiting-offsetting-commas-in-right-node-raising/). Fix example from the post: commas after "jurisdiction of" and after "the laws of".

section: Blog: revisiting-date-and-day
statement: Use date for the point on a calendar that a given day occupies and day for a unit of time; but because using date for day can't cause confusion, don't insist on either. Closing date is fine; don't change closing day to closing date either.
test: Is the word naming a calendar point or a unit of time?
fix: Leave either word unless it causes confusion.
notes: Post date: 2026-07-22. Verified against the post on 5 Nov 2026. Key quotation: "But using date instead of day can't cause confusion, so nothing would be gained by insisting on one over the other." Source: https://www.adamsdrafting.com/revisiting-date-and-day/. Adams calls this his "revised take" on 10.15-10.16 and invites comments; he doesn't say MSCD will change. Reclassified as an elaboration on 5 Nov 2026: the post restates 10.16 (MSCD5 already says nothing is gained by insisting on date or day).

section: Blog: an-exception-to-the-rule-against-also-stating-without-initial-capitals
statement: Exception to the rule that every instance of a defined term takes initial capitals: if a common noun is the defined term for a party (Company, Lender), you may also use that word without initial capitals in its ordinary sense.

trigger.signal: a party's common-noun defined term (Company, Lender) also appearing in lowercase

test: Is the lowercase word a party's common-noun defined term used in its ordinary sense?
fix: Leave it; don't flag it as an inconsistency.
notes: Post date: (not shown). Verified against the post on 5 Nov 2026. Key quotation: "I now propose an exception to that rule" Source: https://www.adamsdrafting.com/an-exception-to-the-rule-against-also-stating-without-initial-capitals/. Adams gives two reasons: such dual use is routine, even unavoidable, and it doesn't create confusion. He doesn't ask for views. Consistent with 6.11, which already notes that a lowercase use may be unavoidable for a common word such as Bank.

section: Blog: language-of-inaction
